name: CodeRabbit
intro: CodeRabbit turned AI code review into a category — free for open source, paid per seat for everything else — reaching an estimated ~$50M annualized run rate and a $1.5B valuation by August 2026. Every publicly reported revenue, funding and adoption number is collected below, each traced back to a source.

modelTitle: How Free Public Reviews Fund $12 Seats.
modelParagraphs: CodeRabbit sells per-seat subscriptions for AI code review. Reviews on public open-source repositories are free indefinitely — a deliberate $10M+ annual investment that makes the product the default check on countless pull requests. Paid plans for private repositories run from around $12 to $24 per user per month, with enterprise agreements adding compliance, on-prem options and priority models.

The open-source wedge is the growth engine: every free review on a public repo is a demonstration to everyone watching that repository, and teams convert to paid seats when they bring the same reviewer into private work. Because CodeRabbit rides on top of GitHub and GitLab rather than replacing them, distribution costs stay low and the product attaches to an existing workflow.
revenueMix: Roughly $12–$24 per user per month for private repositories.

faqs.a: CodeRabbit has not disclosed exact revenue. Third-party estimates put its annualized run rate at roughly $50 million in 2026, implying about $4.2 million of monthly recurring revenue. Treat the figure as an estimate.

A $143 million Series C in August 2026 valued CodeRabbit at $1.5 billion, with Scale Venture Partners, NVIDIA's NVentures and CRV participating. That is up from a $550 million valuation at its $60 million Series B in 2025.

faqs.q: How Does CodeRabbit Price Its Product?
faqs.a: Per-seat subscription plans from roughly $12 to $24 per user per month, plus custom enterprise agreements. Reviews on public open-source repositories are free forever, backed by a company commitment of over $10 million to keep it that way.

faqs.q: Why Is CodeRabbit Free for Open Source?
faqs.a: Free open-source reviews are both mission and acquisition strategy: every public pull request becomes a public demo, and the developers watching those repositories bring CodeRabbit into private, paid work. The Series C committed $10 million or more annually to sustain it.

faqs.q: How Does CodeRabbit Fit With AI Coding Agents Like Cursor or Copilot?
faqs.a: It complements them. Agents write more code faster, which increases the volume of pull requests needing review; CodeRabbit sits in the review step across GitHub, GitLab and other forges rather than inside any one editor.
